effect: The metal fragments joined the hydrated proto-Earth, completing the volatile-bearing young Earth and the chapter. Their arrival order is not fixed, and other hydrogen sources may have contributed.
reaction: It was satisfying to bring the metal and hydrated material together, with the uncertainties made clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Exposing asteroid-core fragments and adding them to the young Earth connected differentiated bodies and iron meteorites to planetary growth.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the hydrated proto-Earth returned no partners, so it offered little direction beyond showing that another ingredient had to be prepared.

surprise.text: Hydrated material could join the growing Earth without implying a cool planet or a surface ocean.

arbitrary.text: Using asteroid-layer fragments rather than rocky planetesimals for the strongly attracting embryo felt somewhat specific, although the automatic correction made the required pairing clear.

continue.text: I would continue: the connections between asteroid interiors, hydrated rock and planetary growth made me curious about how Earth and Theia's story unfolds.
